description:
FOUND s490 (Fable), by the s473t6b review probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s490/probes/t6b/p403.pl (perl 5.40.3 answers p403.perl.out, main p403.main.out, the t6b tree p403.tree.out).  After #403 (s473t6b) 35 of the probe's 37 lines match perl; these two do not:

  -T "/etc"   perl: n=1 [""] (defined)     t6b tree: n=1 undef      (main before #403: n=0, zero values)
  -t 99        perl: n=1 [""] (defined)     t6b tree: n=1 undef

NOT regressions (main left ZERO values for both); residue of the same rule.

1. -T / -B on a directory.  perl stats first; the stat SUCCEEDS, the operand is a directory, the answer is a defined false.  PCL's %p--text-scan opens the path for the first-block scan, the open signals on a directory, %p--scan-first-block answers nil and `*pcl-stat-cache-ok*` is set to nil -- so %p--false reads "the stat failed" and answers undef.  The same happens for an existing but UNREADABLE file (probe it: perl answers undef+EACCES there or ""? -- measure, do not assume).  Fix shape: stat before scanning (through the ONE resolver the scan already uses), and let the scan's failure on an existing file be a defined false.  Also probe `_` after `-T DIR` (does -d _ work?).

2. -t with a numeric operand.  perl pp_fttty: a name that is all digits is an FD NUMBER (`-t 0`, `-t 1`, `-t 99`): isatty(fd) true -> 1, else a DEFINED "" (FT_RETURNNO) -- only a non-numeric name that is no open handle answers undef+EBADF.  PCL's %p--t-impl sends every operand through %p-fileno-impl of a handle NAME, so 99 is "no such handle" -> undef.  Probe `-t 0`, `-t 1`, `-t 2`, `-t "1"`, `-t 99`, `-t "STDIN"`, `-t "nope"` vs perl with stdin/stdout redirected and not.

GUARD: Pl/t/filetest-stack-01.t section 5 (the #403 rows) is the file.  Low priority; both are one-arm fixes in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp (the `cl/` row of WHAT-TO-RUN-WHEN: sweep + op/ io/ companion legs).  Related: #403, #1049 (-t's string rule).
subject: #403 residue (s473t6b review): two filetest falses still answer undef where perl answers a DEFINED "" -- `-T`/`-B` on a DIRECTORY (the stat succeeded; PCL's block scan fails to open it and reads that as a failed stat) and `-t N` with a NUMERIC operand (perl treats it as an fd number: isatty(N), false = "")
